shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving on a large undressed stone slab/monolith
composition divided into horizontal registers by incised lines
a row of repeated, near-identical motifs across the upper zone
horizontal band of dense parallel hatching / fringe-like strokes
figures shown frontally or in profile with limbs/arms indicated
schematic animal or bird-like forms (B) alongside schematic anthropomorphs (A)
arms/forelimbs extending toward a central object
justification: Both are tall stone slabs carved in shallow relief and organised into stacked horizontal registers, each with a row of repeated identical motifs across the top, a hatched/fringed band beneath it, and larger figural elements with outstretched arms below — a genuinely comparable compositional scheme. The biggest difference is subject and handling: A's registers are filled with linear, incised, frontal anthropomorphic figures and small emblem-like signs, whereas B's are dominated by rounded, plastically modelled animal and bird bodies in profile with far fewer, larger elements.
